The more clever and resourceful you prove yourself, the greater your reward.

431955.overview: CAN YOU BREATHE NEW LIFE INTO A DESPERATE CITY THAT'S GASPING FOR AIR AND GRASPING FOR HELP?

454760.overview: King’s Quest VI AGI Demake is a fan-made reimagining of Sierra On-Line’s King’s Quest VI: Heir Today, Gone Tomorrow using the older AGI (Adventure Game Interpreter) engine from the 1980s. While the original 1992 release featured 256-color VGA graphics and a point-and-click interface, this version uses 16-color graphics and a text-based parser interface to replicate the look and feel of Sierra’s earlier adventure games.

456135.overview:
It is the seventh millennium; the Earth is devastated, after centuries of war and multiple nuclear winters that caused a succession of ice ages. Sounds bad? It gets worse: the extreme irradiation has mutated the species, splitting it into four sub-races barely recognizable as human.

Escaping the inhospitable Earth, the factions have established themselves on other planets. A brave new chapter in history unfolds amongst the stars, as mankind begins to play out its potential upon the vast galactic stage: finally, there's enough room to really get serious with maiming, killing and destroying.

Kristor puts the player in command of one of the four factions. Expansion and survival depend on a single vital factor: energy, which is produced by harvesting mineral resources. These come in three varieties (kristor, magnetronium and plasma) scattered throughout the various star systems in the quadrant. Stars may be explored (to prospect for minerals) by sending out unmanned probes; full-scale squadrons can then be launched to claim the system and install a mining unit.

The other three powers don't sit idly by - resources are limited, and competition is fierce. Alliances are formed and dissolved, and battle may be joined when a squadron encounters enemy forces (resulting in a first-person, action-oriented fighting sequence). Construction of ships, probes and mining equipment can be planned and modified according to available energy. All game events are tracked in real time.

The game comes with a cassette tape containing an audio recording, designed to be played in sync with the intro.

456180.overview:
Kakoong is based on the Korean cartoon series of the same name (also known as Kung Fu Jungle Boy). The story takes place on the Cloud Island, a magical realm populated by monsters well-versed in martial arts. The protagonist is a wild boy who protects the island from the schemes of Lord Kojak, who uses his evil super-power of noxious flatulence to subdue the population.

The game is a versus fighter that retains the wacky visuals, environments, and juvenile humor of the original. The versus mode allows the player to select a protagonist from a dozen of characters from the cartoon. Characters mostly fight using traditional punch-and-kick combos; repeatedly using the same move increases the character's proficiency level in it.

465759.overview: This game is a 2D shooter. You have to destroy the enemy's Magnet Power Station with your gun. There are only a few moments before the atomic turbine missile encounters the enemy. As a pilot of a space fighter you have to shoot your way through waves of aliens. You can escape the danger by using warps and special objects - to be collected en route. The aliens will mutate into more dangerous forms the longer they live so don't let the aliens survive.

465761.overview: KaleidoKubes is a puzzle game where players places cubes on a board. The game is meant for two players, either against a human or against the computer, but there is also a practice mode for one player. Each cube is split into four triangles of different colours (blue, green, red, yellow) and to place one on the board the colour of each side has to match the colours of adjacent cubes. Each cube has to connect to at least one other cube. The players earn points for each cube that is placed on the board and the more sides that are connected the more points will be earned. The game is turn based and each player has a limited time (30 or 60 seconds depending on settings) and when it's out the player gets a point penalty and the opponent takes over. For each turn the player has just one cube which can be rotated and if no solution is found, it's possible to pass. The winner is the player with the highest score when the board is filled or when two consecutive combinations of time running out or passes have been made.

465762.overview: With 8 circuits to race on against 2 opponents (one of which can also be human-controlled), this racing game is viewed from above and resembles Super Sprint and early budget-price imitations such as Grand Prix Simulator. Tracks can be raced in the wet, dry or on ice - don't forget to alter the tyre selection to suit. Contact with other cars weakens these tyres and can eventually cause punctures. Each race is of a varying number of laps depending on the track's length and complexity. Sound effects have been sampled, giving the game a realistic sound unusual at the time.

465763.overview: The third entry in the Kick Off series is the first that offers an isometric view instead of the old top-down view. In the game, there are four competitions (World Cup Finals, League, Knock Out Cup and the challenge). There are several options for game speed and ball control to suit both novice and skilled gamers. Each of the 32 teams in the game has a distinct style of play, ensuring that no two games are alike. Each team also has "key players", such as Liberos and Wingers, who play a pivotal role in how that team plays. Kick Off 3 offers two styles of play: Arcade and Simulation. The difference is that in the Arcade mode you can switch off rules to focus purely on reflexes.

469723.overview:
A curious specimen that can compete with Defender of the Freedom (also presented on our website) for the title of the very first South Korean shoot 'em up for PC. Despite some "unsightliness", this game was released not just as a commercial product, but in a real cardboard box, while being a colossal rarity until a certain point, hidden from the public by greedy people. Plot: South Korea is attacked by aliens, and a local pilot, sitting at the helm of the latest fighter, fights alone against them; That's all, but more is not needed to justify what is happening.

The gameplay is quite standard for the subgenre. The perspective of the view is a view from above; The airplane moves forward automatically, but at our command it can go left and right, as well as "brake" and "accelerate". Ammunition in the form of missiles is infinite; Shooting is carried out with the help of the "space" (alas, you can't just hold down this key - you just need to press). There are only six levels, and there are four "lives" (the number of remaining ones, that is, not counting the current one, is displayed in the lower left corner of the screen), and within each of them, which is not very typical for shoot 'em ups, there is also not the smallest margin of safety, expressed in the form of a decreasing red vertical scale along the left border of space; In case of death and in the presence of "attempts", the plane respawns instantly in the same place where it exploded. In the course of the passage, you can collect a variety of bonuses (one of their types, interestingly, is national flags); Apparently, all of them strengthen our attack in one way or another, which is manifested in the addition of some additional effects to its visualization. The contents of the "arsenal", divided into categories, are available for study on the left side of the screen - and it is noticeable that when firing, the stocks of the corresponding contraptions decrease. In addition, there are special items for restoring the "health" of the airplane.

Opponents are represented by various futuristic aircraft and robotic entities of various shapes and sizes; some die almost instantly, while others need to be hit a fair number of times before they explode; It seems that in fact individual enemies move below or above us, since contact with them is sometimes (but quite rarely) harmless. Some adversaries just fly from top to bottom on the screen and, although they shoot, they do not attack us intentionally, so it is possible to avoid them; others, on the contrary, attack precisely purposefully and can even "reverse".

471116.overview: King Kong 10, also known as Guàn Lán Jīngāng: King Kong 10, is an obscure MS-DOS game primarily released in Japan in 1996, although development reportedly took place in China. The game is notable for its quirky premise: a gorilla is kidnapped by a helicopter while playing basketball in the jungle and transported to a city, where he must fend off enemies using his unique abilities.

471146.overview:
A rare Spanish puzzle, divided into several levels and a huge rarity: it became available to humanity only in December 2018.

In the central part of the screen, there are 9 or 16 creatures or objects (angry workers, helmets with eyes, blue gears, anthropomorphic hammers and wrenches...) placed in the shape of a 3x3 or 4x4 square; On any of the four sides of this grid there are three or four pipes, that is, one for each row and column. Control is carried out by the mouse cursor, which by default has the form of a "vertical" screwdriver with a pink handle - when you bring it to the pipe, the color of the latter changes to green (and if the structure is located horizontally, then the tool takes a "lying" position). At the top right there is an image of the latter, on which all the figures are arranged in a certain way, and the task at each level is to repeat this layout on the playing field. This is achieved by clicking on the ends of the pipes, as a result of which the figures in the row or column are shifted one position in the corresponding direction (however, none of them can be inside the structure, therefore, for example, after pressing on the left horizontal pipe, the figure closest to it is the rightmost in this row).

Formally, each stage must be completed within a certain time, while making a predetermined number of cursor clicks (these parameters are displayed before the start); In fact, these restrictions do exist, but, as we managed to find out empirically, they are much more humane. At the same time, as you click on certain pipes, the screwdriver handle begins to take on a yellow, then a red hue, and at some point returns to the original pink - this means that no movement in this particular direction is any longer possible. If you lose, nothing terrible happens - you just reload the same level. It should be noted that the serial number of the latter does not necessarily correspond to the degree of complexity of their passage. Visually, all this is executed in quite pleasing sprite graphics, and even with animation effects (just look at the grimaces that the workers make). The verdict is both easy and difficult (depending on the stage that has fallen), but neither one nor the other causes the slightest irritation; The game is very difficult to let go of - and from the bottom of my heart it is recommended to the widest audience as a short-term intellectual entertainment.

482711.overview: A real-time strategy game follows a Slavic prince rebuilding his strength after an attack on his village. Villages, troops and magic support his campaign, with milk from grazing cows serving as the central economic resource.
